problem:
You are working with a telecom company (mobile + broadband) with ~8M subscribers across multiple regions. Over the past 6 months, the company has seen a 2–3% increase in monthly churn, especially in mid-tenure customers (6–18 months).

The CEO is concerned because:

Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is rising
Network investment is ongoing but not translating into retention
Competitors are offering aggressive pricing bundles
assessment_title: This fits experiment / causal question because the core ask is whether an intervention caused lift, so causal design matters more than raw prediction.
assessment_recap:
Problem type: Experiment / Causal Question
Decision lens: Estimate incremental impact credibly before scaling an action.
Interview recap: We need to understand why churn is moving for subscribers, identify where the risk concentrates, and translate that into a prioritization and intervention plan.
Agent view: Experiment / Causal Question
Framework implication: Start with Objective -> Metric -> Hypotheses before adding custom nodes if needed.
problem_details:
🎯 1) Objective (Business Decision, Horizon, Success)
Decision
Which subscribers should we target this week, and with which retention action, to maximize incremental profit?
Time horizon
Weekly targeting cadence
Primary outcome: 60-day churn / retention
Secondary: 90-day persistence
Success definition
Maximize incremental retained gross profit vs control
Under cost and capacity constraints
📊 2) Business Goal & Metric Definition
Goal
Reduce mid-tenure churn (6–18 months) without destroying margin
Target horizon
0–90 days: operational impact
2–3 quarters: cohort-level retention improvement
Success thresholds
Churn ↓ 0.5–1.0pp in target segment
OR 60-day retention ↑ +3pp
Constraints:
Retention cost ≤ 35% of incremental LTV
ROI ≥ 1.5x
Payback ≤ 3–6 months
⚙️ 3) Decision Logic (Interventions, Constraints, Rules)
Interventions (testable arms)
Price incentive (time-bound credit/discount)
Plan optimization (right-size / bundle)
Service recovery (priority support / tech fix)
Messaging-only (non-monetary)
Budget
Fixed quarterly budget (e.g., $5M) with weekly allocation caps
Capacity
Call center outreach limits
Field technician slots
Campaign delivery limits (SMS/email)
Targeting rules
Act only if expected incremental LTV − cost > 0
Prioritize: ARPU × churn risk × uplift
Exclude:
Active collections / severe open tickets
Customers already in another campaign
Chronic low-margin “serial churners”
🧠 4) Problem Type (Explicit)
Primary: Uplift (who changes behavior if treated)
Secondary: Ranking (fallback if no experimental data)
Supporting: Explanation (drivers for action design)
Model action
Produce a prioritized list of subscribers with recommended intervention per user
🧾 5) Data Scope (Concrete)
Systems
CRM (profile, tenure, plan)
Billing (charges, discounts, payments)
Usage logs (mobile/broadband)
Network telemetry (speed, outages)
Support (tickets, calls)
Time windows
Observation: past 3–6 months
Prediction: next 30–60 days
Backtest: 12–18 months
Segments
Tenure: 0–3, 3–12, 6–18 focus, 18–24, 24+
ARPU: low / mid / high
Product: mobile / broadband / bundle
Geography: proxy for network quality
Known gaps
Competitor pricing (partial)
Off-platform sentiment
True user-level QoE in real time
💰 6) Impact & ROI Definition
Primary metric
Incremental retained revenue / profit (vs control)

ROI

\frac{\text{Incremental LTV saved} - \text{Intervention cost}}{\text{Intervention cost}}
]

Thresholds
ROI ≥ 1.5x
Payback ≤ 3–6 months
Secondary outcomes
High-value churn reduction
Cohort retention curve shift
🧪 7) Experiment Design (Concrete)
Treatment arms
Discount, plan optimization, service recovery, messaging-only
Control
True business-as-usual (no proactive retention)
Randomization unit
Billing account / household (avoid cross-line contamination)
Timing
Weekly eligibility & assignment
Treatment within 72 hours
Measure at 60 days (primary), 90 days (secondary)
Guardrails
Offer cost per save
Margin / ARPU erosion
Complaint & opt-out rate
Downgrade rate
Call center / field capacity
🧑‍💼 8) Audience & Delivery
Audience
CEO / CMO / Head of Retention
Executive concerns
Are we overspending on retention?
Why are valuable users leaving?
What should we do next quarter?
Recommendation style
Where churn is concentrated (segments)
Why it happens (drivers)
What to do (top actions with ROI and constraints)
Output
Ranked target segments
Chosen interventions per segment
Expected impact range + risks
